title: The Cabinet Mission, 1946

endcard.line: Pictures: No 9 Army Film & Photographic Unit (public domain)

segments.say: March nineteen forty-six. Britain sent three cabinet ministers to India with one question: how do you hand over power to a single, united India?
The Cabinet Mission: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A V Alexander. Its plan came out on the sixteenth of May.

anim.title: The plan: three tiers
items: A weak Union: defence, foreign affairs, communications
Provinces grouped in three sections, A, B and C
Groups could have their own constitutions

segments.say: It rejected Pakistan, but offered a loose union. The Centre would handle only defence, foreign affairs and communications. Provinces would sit in three groups, with wide powers.

anim.title: Also
items: A Constituent Assembly, elected by provincial assemblies
An interim government of Indian leaders

segments.say: It also set up a Constituent Assembly, elected by the provincial assemblies, and an interim government.
At first, both the Congress and the Muslim League accepted it. Then they disagreed over whether grouping was compulsory.

items.text: Direct Action Day; violence in Calcutta

segments.say: In July, the League withdrew, and called for Direct Action on the sixteenth of August. Calcutta saw terrible violence. The plan for a united India was finished, though the Constituent Assembly it created met in December.

anim.title: For your answer
items: Three-tier union, groups A, B, C

segments.say: For GS One: the Cabinet Mission's three-tier plan failed, but it gave India the Constituent Assembly that wrote the Constitution.

sources: Statement by the Cabinet Delegation and the Viceroy, 16 May 1946 (Cmd. 6821): Union dealing with foreign affairs, defence and communications; Sections A, B and C; Constituent Assembly elected by provincial legislative assemblies; interim government

quiz.q: Which subjects would the Union handle under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
quiz.why: A weak centre with three subjects.

quiz.q: How was the Constituent Assembly to be elected?

reviewNote: Facts were read against the Cabinet Delegation's statement of 16 May 1946, NCERT Class 12 and the Constituent Assembly Debates. The violence is mentioned once, plainly. Photographs are from 1946, of historical figures. Moving facts: none.
